Rashi on Sanhedrin 15a:10:1.hebrew: אין מועלין בו - דעבד הרי הוא כקרקע, ואין מעילה בקרקע. ובמסכת מעילה (דף יח:) גמר "חטא" "חטא" מתרומה, בפרק הנהנה:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 15a:10:1.english: One is not liable for misuse regarding him - For a slave is [treated] like land, and there is no [liability for] misuse regarding land. And in Tractate Meilah (folio 18b), [the Gemara] derives [this via the verbal analogy of] “sin” [and] “sin” from teruma, in the chapter [entitled] Haneheneh:

Rashi on Sanhedrin 15a:10:2.hebrew: מועלים בשערו - דשערו לאו כגופו, והוה ליה כשאר מטלטלין:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 15a:10:2.english: One is liable for misuse of his hair - For his hair is not [considered] like his body, and it is [thus] like other movable property.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 15a:10:3.english: That is ready to be shorn - For he has already grown long hair, and is fit to have his hair cut.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 15a:10:4.hebrew: ש"מ - פלוגתא דתנאי הוא: לתנא קמא, דאמר לית בהו מעילה — סבר כמחובר דמי, ולענין פדייה נמי בעי עשרה; ולרבן שמעון — כגזוז דמיא:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 15a:10:4.english: Learn from this - It is a dispute between tanna’im: According to the First Tanna, who says [that] there is no [liability for] misuse in it, he holds [that the hair] is considered attached, and with regard to redemption as well, it requires ten [evaluators]; and according to Rabban Shimon, it is considered as [already] shorn.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 15a:11:1.english: Entities that are like land - [Items that are] attached to the land.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 15a:11:2.english: And are not like land - Rather, [they are] like movable property.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 15a:11:3.hebrew: ר"מ מחייב - לישבע על השאר, שהודה מקצת הטענה. אע"ג דאין נשבעין על הקרקעות, כדילפינן בשבועת הדיינים (שבועות דף מב:), הכא, כיון דאין צריכין לקרקע — דעומדות ליבצר הן, כדמוקי ר' יוסי בר חנינא לפולוגתיה — כבצורו' דמיין, ונשבעין:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 15a:11:3.english: Rabbi Meir deems [him] liable - To take an oath regarding the remainder, because he admitted to part of the claim. Even though an oath is not taken concerning land, as we derive in [the chapter entitled] Shevuat HaDayanim (Shevuot 42b), here, since they do not need the land — as they are ready to be harvested, as Rabbi Yosei bar Chanina establishes their dispute — they are considered as if harvested, and an oath is taken.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 15a:12:1.hebrew: לא - התם בענבים, כל כמה דשבקת להו מיכחש כחשי, אבל שערו — אשבוחי משבח. הלכך, אפי' ר' מאיר בשער כרבנן סבירא ליה:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 15a:12:1.english: No - There, with regard to grapes, as long as you leave them [on the vine], they deteriorate; but his hair improves. Therefore, even Rabbi Meir holds in accordance with the Rabbis regarding hair.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 15a:13:1.hebrew: קא פסיק ותני - מתני' רובע סתמא בכ"ג:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 15a:13:1.english: [The Mishnah] categorically teaches - [Our] Mishnah [taught that] an animal that copulated [is judged] without qualification by twenty-three [judges].

Rashi on Sanhedrin 15a:13:2.hebrew: לא שנא - שור שרבע אדם זכר, ולא שנא שור שרבע אשה נקבה, דנפקא לן תרוייהו מקראי בפרק ארבע מיתות (לקמן סנהדרין נד:) שהן בסקילה, ותנא דמתני' מרבי להו לכ"ג:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 15a:13:2.english: There is no difference - [Whether it is] an ox that copulated with a male human, and there is no difference [whether it is] an ox that copulated with a female human, for we derive both of them from verses in the chapter [entitled] Arba Mitot (below, Sanhedrin 54b) that they are [punished] by stoning, and the Tanna of our Mishnah includes them [both to be judged] by twenty-three [judges].

Rashi on Sanhedrin 15a:13:3.hebrew: בשלמא רובע נקבה - כתיב ביה כ"ג, דכתיב: "והרגת את האשה ואת הבהמה" — איתקש בהמה לאשה, ודיני נפשות נפקינן לקמן בעשרים ושלשה:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 15a:13:3.english: Granted, [an animal that] copulated with a female - Twenty-three [judges] are written concerning it, as it is written: "And you shall kill the woman and the animal" — the animal is juxtaposed with the woman, and capital cases, we derive below [are decided] by twenty-three.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 15a:13:4.hebrew: אלא רובע זכר - מנלן דבעי כ"ג:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 15a:13:4.english: But [an animal] that copulated with a male - From where do we [derive] that it requires twenty-three [judges]?

Rashi on Sanhedrin 15a:14:1.english: As it is written: “Whoever lies,” etc. - And from this [verse] we derive in [the chapter entitled] Arba Mitot regarding [an animal that] mounts a male.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 15a:14:2.hebrew: דאם אינו ענין - לאדם הבא על הבהמה, דהא קרא אחרינא כתיב (ויקרא כ׳:ט״ו): איש אשר יתן שכבתו וגו':
Rashi on Sanhedrin 15a:14:2.english: That if it is not relevant - [With respect] to a man who copulates with an animal, for another verse is written (Leviticus 20:15): “If a man has carnal relations, etc.”

Rashi on Sanhedrin 15a:14:3.hebrew: תניהו ענין לנשכב - למביא בהמה עליו. ומדאפקיה בלשון שוכב — לידון כשוכב: מה בא על הבהמה, הוא והיא בכ"ג, כדילפינן מ"ואת הבהמה תהרוגו" (שם), דאיתקש בהמה לאדם — אף מביא בהמה עליו, שניהם בכ"ג:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 15a:14:3.english: Apply it to the matter of one who is lain with - To one who brings an animal upon himself. And since [the Torah] expressed it with the term “lies,” [this is so that he will] be judged like one who lies [actively]: Just as [in the case of] one who has intercourse with an animal, he and it [are judged] by twenty-three [judges], as we derive from “and you shall slay the animal” (ibid.), where the animal is compared to the person — so too, [in the case of] one who brings an animal upon himself, both of them [are judged] by twenty-three [judges].

Rashi on Sanhedrin 15a:1:1.hebrew: האומר ערך כלי זה עלי נותן דמיו - כמו שהוא שוה, דיודע הוא שאין לומר לשון ערך לכלי ואין ערכו קצוב, וגמר ואמר לשם דמים, דאין אדם מוציא דבריו לבטלה:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 15a:1:1.english: One who says: "The valuation of this utensil is upon me," gives its value - As much as it is worth; for he knows that one does not use the term "valuation" for a utensil and its valuation is not fixed, and he resolved and spoke for the sake of monetary value, for a person does not utter his words in vain.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 15a:1:2.english: Valuations that are movable property - [This] implies that the valuations [themselves] are movable.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 15a:2:1.hebrew: במתפיס מטלטלין לערכו - שאומר: "ערכי עלי", ונתחייב ערך הקצוב לפי שניו, והיה לו מטלטלין, ואמר: "הרי אלו לערכי", וחלה עליהן קדושה, ובא לפדותן — צריך ג' להוציאן מיד הקדש:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 15a:2:1.english: In [the case of] one who associates movable property with his valuation - Where one says, "My valuation is upon me," and became obligated in the valuation fixed according to his age, and he had movable property and said, "Behold, these are for my valuation," and sanctity took effect upon them, and [now] comes to redeem them — he requires three [assessors] to release them from the possession of the Temple treasury.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 15a:3:1.hebrew: ר' אבהו אומר באומר ערכי עלי - ואינו פורע, ובא כהן למשכנו ומצא לו מטלטלין. והכי קאמר: הערכין — דהיינו ערך אדם, ובא ליתן מטלטלין — נגבין בשלשה שמאין:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 15a:3:1.english: Rabbi Abbahu says: In [the case of] one who says, “My valuation is incumbent upon me” - And he does not pay, and the priest came to seize collateral from him and found movable property belonging to him. And this is what [the Mishnah] means to say: Valuations — that is, the valuation of a person, and he comes to give movable property — are collected by three appraisers.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 15a:3:2.hebrew: בשלמא לאפוקי מהקדש - כגון דרב גידל ורב חסדא, הוא דבעי שלשה; דכיון דחל עליו הקדש, לא ניפוק עד שיפדנו בשויו:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 15a:3:2.english: Granted, to take [property] out of consecration - Such as [in the cases of] Rav Giddel and Rav Ḥisda, that is where it requires three [assessors]; for since consecration has taken effect upon it, it should not leave [consecration] until he redeems it at its value.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 15a:3:3.english: But to bring [property] in - Such as [the case] of Rabbi Abbahu.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 15a:4:1.english: Bringing in as well, perhaps they will err - And take it for the Temple treasury at more than its value.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 15a:6:1.english: One for itself - That we require a priest.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 15a:6:2.hebrew: מיעוט אחר מיעוט - דכולהו ממעטי ישראל, דמשמע כהן ולא ישראל:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 15a:6:2.english: A restrictive expression after a restrictive expression - For all of them exclude an Israelite, as it implies a priest and not an Israelite.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 15a:7:1.hebrew: ואימא חמשה כהנים וחמשה ישראל - בעינן, דקמא לגופיה, ושני לו הוי מיעוט אחר מיעוט, ושלישי הדר איצטריך לגופיה דניהוי כהן; דכיון דאיתרבי ליה ממיעוט אחר מיעוט דאפילו ישראל, כי הדר כתב כהן — דוקא כתביה, דלאו מיעוט אחר מיעוט הוא, דהא שני לאו מיעוט הוא אלא ריבוי. וכן כולם: חד דווקא, וחד הוי מיעוט אחר מיעוט:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 15a:7:1.english: And say five priests and five Israelites - We require [them], for the first [mention] is for itself, and the second to it is a restriction following a restriction, and the third is needed once again for itself, that it be a priest. For since it was included through a restriction following a restriction that even an Israelite [is valid], when it writes “priest” again, it wrote it specifically [as a priest], for it is not a restriction following a restriction, as the second is not a restriction, but an inclusion. And so too with all of them: one is specifically [a priest], and one is a restriction following a restriction.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 15a:8:1.hebrew: ואדם כיוצא בהן - כקרקעות, דבעי נמי תשע וכהן לשומו:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 15a:8:1.english: And a person is like them - Like land, as it also requires nine [judges] and a priest to appraise him.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 15a:8:2.english: And a slave is compared to land - [As it is written:] “And you may hold them as an inheritance [for your children after you, to inherit as a possession]” (Leviticus 25:46).

Rashi on Sanhedrin 15a:9:1.hebrew: שער העומד ליגזוז - והקדישו, ובא לפדותו בשויו — שעושין משער אדם נפה, וקילקלי, וחבק:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 15a:9:1.english: Hair that is ready to be shorn - [Where one] consecrated it and came to redeem it at its value — for people make from human hair a sieve, a breastband, and a girth.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 15a:9:2.hebrew: כגזוז דמי - והוו להו מטלטלין, ובשלשה:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 15a:9:2.english: [Is it] considered as shorn - And they are [thus] movable property, and [appraised] by three [judges].

Tosafot on Sanhedrin 15a:10:1.hebrew: אין מועלין - כאן משמע דאין מעילה במחובר, ובהדיא אמרי' הכי במסכת מעילה (דף יד:). וקשה לפי' רשב"ם דבפ' המוכר את הספינה (ב"ב דף עט. ושם), גבי מקדיש דקתני: "מועלין בבור", ופי': כגון שהצניע חפצים בבור — ולא יתכן, דהיינו מחובר; אלא שעקר חוליא מן הבור ונהנה ממנה:
Tosafot on Sanhedrin 15a:10:1.english: "One is not liable for misuse" - Here it is implied that there is no [liability for] misuse regarding [property that is] attached [to the ground], and we explicitly say so in tractate Meilah (14b). And this poses a difficulty for the explanation of the Rashbam in the chapter [entitled] HaMokher Et HaSefinah (Bava Batra 79a and there), regarding [one who] consecrates [a cistern], where [the Mishnah] teaches: "[Deriving benefit from] a cistern is subject to misuse," and he explained: For example, where he stored items in the cistern — and [yet] this cannot be, as that is [property] attached [to the ground]! Rather, [it must be a case] where he detached a block [or rim] from the cistern and derived benefit from it.

Tosafot on Sanhedrin 15a:12:1.hebrew: בענבים העומדים ליבצר - תימה, דבפרק נערה (כתובות דף נא: ושם) פריך גבי "זיל הב ליה מתמרי דעל בודיא": "סוף סוף, כל העומד לגזוז כגזוז דמי?", ומשני: "דצריכי לדיקלא קאמינא". ומאי פריך? והא רבנן דהכא לית להו הך סברא! וי"ל, דגבי בעל חוב מודה דלא גבי מדבר העומד לגזוז, דלא סמכא דעתיה. ועוד, פר"ח דהתם פריך משום דבפרק הכונס (ב"ק דף נט:) פסיק רב כרבי שמעון, דאמר: "אכלה פירות גמורים — משלמת פירות גמורים, ואין שמין אותן אגב שדה", משמע דכבצורות דמיין:
Tosafot on Sanhedrin 15a:12:1.english: "With grapes that are ready to be picked" - [This is] puzzling, for in the chapter [entitled] Na'arah (Ketubot 51b and there), [the Gemara] objects with regard to [the ruling]: "Go give him from the dates that are upon the mat": "Ultimately, is whatever stands to be harvested not considered as [already] harvested?", [and the Gemara answers:] "I said [this of dates] that [still] need the palm tree." And why did [the Gemara] object? Behold, the Rabbis here do not accept this reasoning! And one can say that with regard to a creditor, [the Rabbis] concede that he does not collect from something that stands to be harvested, because he did not rely [upon it]. And furthermore, Rabbeinu Chananel explained that there [the Gemara] objected because in the chapter [entitled] HaKones (Bava Kamma 59b), Rav ruled in accordance with Rabbi Shimon, who said: "[If an animal] ate fully ripe fruits, [its owner] pays for fully ripe fruits, and they do not evaluate them as part of the field" — which implies that they are considered as if [already] harvested.

Tosafot on Sanhedrin 15a:14:1.hebrew: אם אינו ענין לשוכב כו' - ומהכא נמי בפ' ד' מיתות (לקמן סנהדרין דף נד:) ילפינן אזהרה לנשכב: מה שוכב ענש והזהיר כו'. ותימה: ר' אבהו דפליג עלה התם — כ"ג מנא לן? וכן רבי שמעון, דדריש מיניה התם (ד' ס.) דבני נח מוזהרים על כישוף, מדאיתקש לשוכב עם בהמה; וכן לבן עזאי, דגמר מיניה דמכשף בסקילה בההוא פירקא (דף סז:)? וי"ל: דאי משום הקיש, הל"ל קרא ד"איש כי יתן את שכבתו בבהמה" גבי מכשפה; הלכך קרא ד"כל שוכב" מיותר לנשכב, כדדרשינן:
Tosafot on Sanhedrin 15a:14:1.english: “If it is not [needed for] the matter of the one who lies, etc.” - And from here as well, in the chapter [entitled] Arba Mitot (below, Sanhedrin 54b), we derive the warning for the passive participant: Just as for the active participant [the Torah] punished and warned, etc. And it is puzzling: [According to] Rabbi Abbahu, who disagrees with it there — from where do we derive twenty-three? And similarly, [as for] Rabbi Shimon, who expounds from it there (60a) that the descendants of Noah are warned against sorcery, since it is juxtaposed with “Whoever lies with an animal”; and similarly, according to Ben Azzai, who learns from it that a sorcerer is [executed] by stoning in that chapter (67b) — [how can the verse be considered redundant]? And one can say: If it were [only] because of the juxtaposition, Scripture should have stated the verse of “a man who gives his lying with an animal” next to [the verse of] a sorceress; therefore, the verse of “Whoever lies” is redundant for [the case of] the passive participant, as we expound.

Tosafot on Sanhedrin 15a:1:1.hebrew: האומר ערך כלי עלי נותן דמיו - בפ"ק דערכין (דף ה.) מוקי לה כר' מאיר, דאמר: אין אדם מוציא דבריו לבטלה. ותימה: דבפרק השולח (גיטין דף לח: ושם) אמר רב: "המקדיש עבדו יצא לחירות, מאי טעמא? גופיה לא קדיש כו'", משמע התם דהיינו דלא כר"מ, דלדידי' קדוש לדמיו! ונראה, דההיא דערכין — אליבא דר' מאיר קאמר רב, וליה לא סבירא ליה. וכן משמע התם (ערכין דף ה.), דפריך: "לר"מ פשיטא!" ואי אתא למימר דסבר כר' מאיר, מאי פריך פשיטא? אלא משמע דלא סבר כרבי מאיר, אלא קאמר דלר"מ נותן דמיו. א"נ, איכא ב' לישני דרב בגיטין (דף לח:): חד במקדיש, וחד במפקיר:
Tosafot on Sanhedrin 15a:1:1.english: "One who says: The valuation of a utensil is upon me, gives its value" - In the first chapter of Arakhin (5a), [the Gemara] establishes this [statement] in accordance with Rabbi Meir, who said: A person does not utter his words in vain. And this is puzzling: For in the chapter [entitled] HaSholach (Gittin 38b and there), Rav said: "One who consecrates his slave, [the slave] is emancipated. What is the reason? His body cannot be consecrated, etc." — which implies there that this is not in accordance with Rabbi Meir, for according to his [Rabbi Meir's] view, he is consecrated for his monetary value! And it appears that that [statement] in Arakhin, Rav stated according to [the opinion of] Rabbi Meir, but he himself does not hold [in accordance with it]. And so it is implied there (Arakhin 5a), where [the Gemara] asks: "According to Rabbi Meir, isn't it obvious?" And if [Rav] had come to say that he holds in accordance with Rabbi Meir, why would [the Gemara] ask: "Isn't it obvious?" Rather, it implies that [Rav] did not hold in accordance with Rabbi Meir, but rather stated that according to Rabbi Meir, he gives its value. Alternatively, there are two versions of Rav's [statement] in Gittin (38b): one [version] where he consecrates, and one where he renounces ownership.

Tosafot on Sanhedrin 15a:8:1.hebrew: אדם מי קדוש - וא"ת: ולוקמא בעבד, דקדוש — כדאמרינן בסמוך דמועלין בשערו, ואמר בהשולח (שם): "המקדיש נכסיו והיו בהם עבדים, אין הגזברים רשאין להוציאם לחירות"? וי"ל: ד"אדם" לא משמע ליה דקאי אעבד. אי נמי, הכא פריך אליבא דרב, דאמר (שם): "המקדיש עבדו יצא לחירות":
Tosafot on Sanhedrin 15a:8:1.english: Can a person be consecrated? - And if you say: Let [the Gemara] establish [the mishna] with regard to a slave, who can be consecrated — as we say nearby that [the laws of] misuse [me’ilah] apply to his hair, and it says in [the chapter entitled] HaSholei’ach (there): "One who consecrates his property and there were slaves among them, the treasurers are not permitted to manumit them"? And one can say: [The term] "a person" did not imply to [the Gemara] that it refers to a slave. Alternatively, here [the Gemara] challenges according to [the opinion of] Rav, who said (there): "One who consecrates his slave goes out to freedom."

Tosafot on Sanhedrin 15a:9:1.hebrew: שער העומד ליגזוז - אף על גב דמעילה ילפינן מתרומה, ולענין תרומה לא אמרינן "כל העומד לקצור כקצור דמי" — דלענין האי לא ילפינן מתרומה, ד"תמעול מעל" ריבה, כדדרשינן במעילה (דף יח:) לגבי כמה דברים:
Tosafot on Sanhedrin 15a:9:1.english: Hair that is ready to be shorn - Even though we derive [the laws of] misuse from teruma, and with regard to teruma we do not say that whatever is ready to be reaped is deemed as reaped — [nevertheless,] regarding this [matter] we do not derive from teruma, for "shall commit a trespass" [tim’ol ma’al] is an amplification, as we expound in Me’ila (18b) regarding several matters.
